## 2. Scene claims to verify (5)

These scenes state how a rule or product works. Check the explanation text against the listed sources.

### `ch1-e1-s1` — Where did it go?

> Gross pay is what you earn. Net pay, or take-home pay, is what's left after your employer withholds federal income tax, Social Security, Medicare and often state tax. Withholding isn't extra cost; it's paying your tax a little at a time. Claiming "exempt" stops the income-tax part, but you can only do that if you expect to owe no federal income tax at all. Otherwise, you owe it all at once later.

- Form W-4: Employee's Withholding Certificate (instructions on claiming exemption) (Internal Revenue Service) — https://www.irs.gov/forms-pubs/about-form-w-4

### `ch1-e1-s3` — The pre-checked box

> Checking is for spending; savings is for keeping. Keeping them apart makes it harder to spend your cushion by accident, and a high-yield savings account pays far more interest. Overdraft "coverage" sounds helpful, but each time it covers a purchase you can be charged a fee. For everyday debit-card purchases and ATM withdrawals, banks need you to opt in first, which is why the box was pre-checked.

- What are overdraft fees and how do they work? (Consumer Financial Protection Bureau) — https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/what-is-an-overdraft-fee-en-1053/

### `ch1-e3-s3a` — Fee, fee, fee

> Overdraft fees are flat charges for small shortfalls, so they're extremely expensive for what they are. Three fixes: turn off overdraft coverage for debit purchases so they're declined instead, link savings to cover shortfalls, and set a low-balance alert. Banks often refund a fee if you ask politely, especially the first time. It never hurts to ask.

- What are overdraft fees and how do they work? (Consumer Financial Protection Bureau) — https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/what-is-an-overdraft-fee-en-1053/

### `ch1-e3-s3b` — Priya's $105 mistake

> Overdraft fees are flat charges for small shortfalls, so they're extremely expensive for what they are. Three fixes: turn off overdraft coverage for debit purchases so they're declined instead, link savings to cover shortfalls, and set a low-balance alert. ### `ch1-e4-s3` — Guaranteed 12%

> Real investments that can earn a lot can also lose a lot; that's the trade-off between risk and return. Anyone promising high returns with no risk is either mistaken or lying. Bank savings are protected by FDIC insurance if a bank fails, but many money apps aren't banks. Red flags: "guaranteed," "limited spots," pressure to hurry and crowds of comments bragging about gains.

- Deposit Insurance (Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation) — https://www.fdic.gov/resources/deposit-insurance

## 3. Illustrative values and conventions — sanity-check only (13)

These are labeled "illustrative" in the game. They should be realistic, not exact.

| Key | Value | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `taxYear` | 2026 | Tax year the brackets below describe |
| `stateTaxRate` | 4% | Flat stand-in for state and local income tax — Real state taxes range from zero to progressive brackets above 10%. The game uses one flat rate. |
| `typicalCardApr` | 22% | Typical credit-card APR — Rounded to a typical recent level. Check the latest G.19 before citing it as a statistic. |
| `cardMinimumPercent` | 1% | Minimum payment, share of balance (paid on top of that month's interest) — A common issuer formula. Real formulas vary by issuer. |
| `cardMinimumFloor` | 25 | Smallest minimum payment — Varies by issuer. |
| `cardLateFee` | 30 | Late fee on a missed card payment — Late-fee rules have been changing; keep illustrative. |
| `overdraftFee` | 35 | Overdraft fee per item — Long a common figure at large banks; many banks have since cut or dropped it. |
| `hysaApy` | 3.5% | High-yield savings account APY — Online savings rates move with the Fed. Keep illustrative. |
| `bankSavingsApy` | 0.4% | Typical big-bank savings account APY |
| `longRunInflation` | 3% | Inflation rate used in long-run examples |
| `stockLongRunReturn` | 7% | Long-run nominal return used for a diversified stock index fund in examples — Not a promise. Real returns vary a lot from year to year. |
| `emergencyFundMonthsGoal` | 3 | Starter emergency-fund goal, in months of essential expenses — Common guidance is 3-6 months; the game starts players at 3. |
| `housingShareGuideline` | 30% | Rule-of-thumb share of income for housing — A common planning guideline, not a law. Often stated against gross income; the game compares it with take-home pay to be conservative. |
